title: Design Instagram - Photo Sharing Platform
question: Design Instagram with 500M users posting 100M photos daily. Requirements: 1) Users upload photos with captions and hashtags, 2) Follow other users and see their posts in feed, 3) Like and comment on posts, 4) Search by hashtags and users, 5) Image storage and CDN delivery, 6) News feed generation in <200ms, 7) Handle viral posts (1M likes in minutes). Discuss: using object storage (S3) for images with CDN (CloudFront) for global delivery, storing image metadata in database (post_id, user_id, caption, hashtags, created_at), implementing fan-out on write for feed generation (when user posts, write to all followers' feeds), using Redis for hot feed cache, implementing hashtag indexing with Elasticsearch for search, storing likes/comments count with eventual consistency, using message queue for async operations (notifications, analytics), implementing database sharding by user_id, using read replicas for feed reads, and handling viral posts with rate limiting and caching.

title: Design E-Commerce Platform - Amazon-like System
question: Design e-commerce platform handling 10K orders/second. Requirements: 1) Product catalog with search and filters, 2) Shopping cart with session management, 3) Order placement with payment processing, 4) Inventory management across warehouses, 5) Real-time stock updates, 6) Order tracking and notifications, 7) Flash sales support (10x normal traffic). Discuss: using Elasticsearch for product search with faceted filtering, caching product catalog in Redis with TTL, storing cart in Redis with session expiration, implementing optimistic locking for inventory (check stock, reserve, confirm), using message queue for order processing pipeline (payment → inventory → shipping → notification), implementing event sourcing for order state, using database sharding by user_id or order_id, read replicas for product reads, implementing rate limiting for flash sales, using CDN for product images, and handling distributed transactions with Saga pattern.

title: Design Hotel/Flight Booking System
question: Design booking system preventing double bookings. Requirements: 1) Search available hotels/flights by location and date, 2) Real-time availability display, 3) Prevent double booking (two users booking same room), 4) Hold reservation for 10 minutes during payment, 5) Handle cancellations and refunds, 6) Peak load during holidays (100x normal), 7) Global distribution (multi-region). Discuss: using distributed locks (Redis, Zookeeper) for booking atomicity, implementing optimistic locking with version column, creating inventory table with available_count column (decrement atomically), using pessimistic locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE) during booking, implementing reservation timeout with scheduled cleanup job, storing booking states (pending, confirmed, cancelled) with state machine, using message queue for async processing (confirmation emails, refunds), caching search results with short TTL, implementing database partitioning by region, using read replicas for search queries, and handling payment failures with compensation logic.

title: Design Distributed Cache System
question: Design distributed cache like Redis/Memcached. Requirements: 1) Store key-value pairs in memory, 2) Horizontal scalability (add/remove nodes), 3) High availability (node failures), 4) LRU eviction policy, 5) TTL support, 6) Consistent hashing for key distribution, 7) Handle network partitions. Discuss: implementing consistent hashing ring for key distribution (minimize data movement when nodes added/removed), storing data in hash map with linked list for LRU, using gossip protocol for node discovery and failure detection, implementing replication (master-slave) for availability, handling split-brain with quorum-based writes, using bloom filters for negative cache lookups, implementing write-ahead log for persistence, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous replication, handling cache stampede with mutex, and monitoring cache hit ratio.

title: Design Distributed Job Scheduler
question: Design distributed task scheduler for running millions of cron jobs. Requirements: 1) Schedule jobs at specific times or intervals, 2) Distributed execution across workers, 3) Job retry on failure, 4) Job dependencies (job B runs after job A), 5) Priority-based execution, 6) Job monitoring and alerts, 7) Handle worker failures gracefully. Discuss: storing jobs in database with next_run_time index, using priority queue for job ordering, implementing leader election (using Zookeeper) for scheduler coordination, distributing jobs to workers via message queue, using heartbeat for worker health monitoring, storing job execution history for monitoring, implementing exponential backoff for retries, handling dependencies with DAG representation, using distributed locks for job execution (prevent duplicate runs), implementing job timeout with cleanup, and supporting both one-time and recurring jobs.

title: Design Centralized Logging System
question: Design centralized logging for microservices. Requirements: 1) Collect logs from 100+ services, 2) Handle 1M logs/second, 3) Full-text search on logs, 4) Retention (30 days hot, 1 year archive), 5) Real-time dashboards and alerts, 6) Distributed tracing correlation, 7) Cost-effective storage. Discuss: using log shippers (Filebeat) on each service to forward logs, sending to message queue (Kafka) for buffering and durability, processing logs with stream processor (Logstash) for parsing and enrichment, storing in Elasticsearch for search and aggregation, implementing time-based indices (daily) for efficient querying and deletion, archiving old logs to S3, using Kibana for dashboards, implementing alerting on log patterns, storing trace IDs in logs for correlation, using sampling for high-volume services, and implementing log levels for filtering.

title: Design API Gateway for Microservices
question: Design API Gateway handling 100K requests/second. Requirements: 1) Route requests to appropriate microservices, 2) Authentication and authorization, 3) Rate limiting per client, 4) Request/response transformation, 5) Circuit breaking and retry, 6) Caching responses, 7) Monitoring and logging. Discuss: implementing reverse proxy for routing based on URL patterns, using JWT for authentication with Redis token cache, implementing token bucket algorithm for rate limiting in Redis, caching responses in Redis with cache-control headers, using circuit breaker (Hystrix/Resilience4j) for fault tolerance, implementing request batching for efficiency, using connection pooling to backends, load balancing across service instances, implementing retry with exponential backoff, logging all requests with correlation IDs, monitoring latency and error rates, and handling service discovery with Eureka/Consul.

title: Design Metrics Collection System
question: Design time-series metrics system like Prometheus. Requirements: 1) Collect metrics from services (CPU, memory, requests), 2) Store 1M metrics/second, 3) Query and aggregate metrics efficiently, 4) Retention (7 days full resolution, 90 days downsampled), 5) Alerting on metric thresholds, 6) Visualize metrics in dashboards. Discuss: using push vs pull model for metric collection (pull for service discovery), storing metrics in time-series database (Prometheus, InfluxDB), implementing metric labels for multi-dimensional querying, using columnar storage for efficient aggregation, downsampling old data (1-minute → 5-minute → 1-hour), implementing retention policies with automatic deletion, creating alerting rules with threshold conditions, using recording rules for pre-computed aggregations, implementing federation for scaling, and optimizing storage with compression.

title: Design Authentication Service - SSO System
question: Design single sign-on (SSO) authentication service. Requirements: 1) Centralized authentication for 50 applications, 2) Support multiple auth methods (password, OAuth, SAML), 3) Session management across applications, 4) MFA support, 5) Password reset and account recovery, 6) Audit logging, 7) Handle 10K logins/minute. Discuss: implementing OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect for SSO, storing user credentials with bcrypt hashing, using JWT for stateless authentication, storing sessions in Redis with sliding expiration, implementing refresh tokens for long-lived sessions, supporting TOTP for MFA with secret storage, using email/SMS for password reset with time-limited tokens, implementing rate limiting on login attempts, storing audit logs for compliance, using HTTPS with HSTS, implementing CSRF protection, supporting social login (Google, Facebook), and handling account lockout after failed attempts.

title: Design Real-Time Leaderboard System
question: Design leaderboard for gaming platform with 10M players. Requirements: 1) Update scores in real-time, 2) Query top 100 players globally, 3) Get player's rank and nearby players, 4) Multiple leaderboards (daily, weekly, all-time), 5) Handle score ties, 6) Support leaderboard filtering (by region, level), 7) Reset daily/weekly boards at midnight. Discuss: using Redis sorted sets for leaderboard storage, player_id as member and score as score value, using ZADD for atomic score updates, ZREVRANGE for top N, ZREVRANK for player rank, implementing composite score (score + timestamp) for tie-breaking, creating separate sorted sets per leaderboard type and region, using scheduled job for resetting time-based boards, implementing pagination for leaderboard viewing, caching leaderboard snapshots for read-heavy loads, and handling high write throughput with write batching.
